Saga first-year outcomes: interpretation and coverage

## Reading the outcome tables

Tables 3–4 report first-year ITT and TOT estimates from two trials. ITT measures the effect of being offered tutoring; TOT estimates the effect of participation using assignment as an instrument. These are two views of the same trials, not independent replications. Standard errors and outcome-specific sample counts remain attached to each estimate.

## Units and interpretation

Test-score estimates use study-sample standard deviations; GPA uses grade points. Course-failure and ever-arrested values are stored as fractions, not percentage points. Negative estimates do not have a universal meaning: fewer failures or arrests differ from lower test scores. The suspension table label does not unambiguously distinguish days from events, so those four estimates have no assigned outcome unit and are unsuitable for normalized comparisons.

## Shared source statistics

The source tables also report control means, estimated control-complier means and false-discovery-rate q-values. Those are not interchangeable with effect estimates or ordinary p-values; they are not yet supplied as structured fields here. A control-complier mean is an estimate, not an observed control-group average.

## Source and limits

[Final AER article](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.20210434), Tables 3–4, pp. 749–750. These estimates do not include every later-year or pooled analysis. The trial costs use a separate nominal-budget accounting basis; these tables calculate no benefit-cost ratio.
Academic, attendance, disciplinary and arrest estimates from two randomized Chicago tutoring trials. Each estimate retains its study, uncertainty and source context.
